item: Kani H6 inherits #[kani::unwind(4)] from H5; no new loop introduced by the trailing-bytes check
reason: The trailing-bytes check at the post-fix crates/vb_storage/src/codec/payload.rs:69-71 is a single if + Err return: `if bytes.len() > payload_end { return Err(JournalError::TrailingBytes { trailing: bytes.len() - payload_end }); }`. There is no loop, no recursion, no heap allocation on this path. The existing H5 harness (kani_harness_digest_before_postcard at crates/vb_storage/src/kani_postcard_envelope_wire.rs:271-337) already uses #[kani::unwind(4)] for the same 60-byte header + arbitrary payload_len shape; H6 inherits the same bound. The trailing-byte count is concrete (1..=8) per proof-strategy §2.5 A-003: 'kani::any() can construct a valid 60-byte header + payload + trailing bytes without exceeding #[kani::unwind(4)]'.
impact: The Kani H6 verification explores all reachable states up to #[kani::unwind(4)] which is sufficient for the trailing-bytes path. If the production code is later modified to introduce a loop on the trailing-bytes path, the bound must be re-evaluated.
compensating_evidence: cargo check -p vb_storage --features legacy-kani passes (0 errors, 0 warnings). The H6 file syntax is correct. The kani::any() over header/payload gives full symbolic coverage; only the trailing-byte count is concrete (1..=8) to bound the unwinding.
expiry: re-evaluate if production code adds a loop on the trailing-bytes path

item: Verus bridge arm new parameter `expected_payload_end: u32` is the top-level bridge parameter approach
reason: The proof-strategy §3 reduction justifications explicitly states: 'The Verus bridge arm uses expected_payload_end as a top-level bridge parameter. Per contracts/type-contracts.md §4.3: the planner may extend SpecRecordEnvelope to carry payload_len, OR hoist expected_payload_end as a top-level bridge parameter. The latter is the minimum-fuss template (no spec surface change beyond the new arm).' The proof-writer followed the minimum-fuss template: added expected_payload_end: u32 as a new top-level parameter to the assume_specification[ production::decode_record ] bridge and the production-mirror decode_record exec fn. The alternative (extending SpecRecordEnvelope) was rejected to keep the spec surface change minimal.
impact: The bridge signature is now `assume_specification[ production::decode_record ](bytes: Vec<u8>, expected_magic: u32, max_payload_len: u32, expected_payload_end: u32, header_ok: bool, decoded_envelope: SpecRecordEnvelope, decode_ok: bool, parity_ok: bool)`. All 4 existing wrappers (wrapper_encode_record_ok is unaffected; wrapper_encode_record_family_mismatch, wrapper_encode_record_payload_too_large, wrapper_decode_record_ok, wrapper_decode_record_bad_magic, wrapper_decode_record_parity_mismatch) were updated to pass the new parameter (0u32 for unchanged-arms; the new wrapper_decode_record_trailing_bytes passes the parameter through from its own decode_ok parameter).
compensating_evidence: verus --crate-type=lib verification/verus/vb-vzcuf-PS-003.rs reports 25 verified proofs with 0 errors. The new wrapper_decode_record_trailing_bytes is one of the 25 verified.
expiry: permanent until SpecRecordEnvelope is extended (not currently planned)
